newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Radical Chechen says he behind Russia bomb attacks.
newsitem.headline: Radical Chechen says he behind Russia bomb attacks.

text.p: Radical Chechen rebel commander Salman Raduyev has claimed responsibility for two recent bomb attacks in southern Russia in which four people died.

"The explosions in Armavir and Pyatigorsk were carried out on my personal order...This is a new phase of the Russian-Chechen war," Raduyev told NTV commercial television's Itogi news programme in an interview broadcast on Sunday.

Nearly two weeks ago a powerful bomb killed two people in Armavir, which is near Chechnya. Another two people were killed and 20 wounded last Monday when a bomb badly damaged the railway station in the spa resort of Pyatigorsk, also near the breakaway region.

Raduyev, a flamboyant but isolated figure who is not part of Chechnya's post-war separatist leadership, has several times vowed to attack Russian targets over Moscow's refusal to recognise his country's independence.
But it is not clear how many armed supporters he has, although Chechnya, where rebels fought a 21-month war with Russian troops sent to crush an independence bid, is still awash with weapons.
Russian police have detained two Chechen women suspected of organising the Pyatigorsk blast.
"Those two women have been detained because of me because I gave the order," said Raduyev.
"If a single hair of their heads is harmed Russia will regret it," he said with characteristic bravado, adding that he was planning further attacks in Russia.
Last week Itar-Tass had quoted Raduyev as claiming responsibility for the Armavir explosion but more moderate Chechen leaders said they doubted he had really been behind the attack.
Some Russian and Chechen officials have questioned Raduyev's sanity, though in Sunday's television interview he cheerfully dismissed suggestions that he might need psychiatric help.
Raduyev, wanted by Russian police for masterminding a bloody armed raid in the Russian region of Dagestan bordering Chechnya last January, was reported killed in an ambush last year.
He later resurfaced, saying he had been seriously hurt but had undergone plastic surgery in Germany. His face was barely recognisable.
The situation around Chechnya has deteriorated badly in the past week.

Apart from the two bomb incidents, unidentified gunmen shot dead a senior official in the neighbouring region of Ingushetia and Russian police fought a brief pre-dawn skirmish with a group of what they said were 20 Chechen fighters just outside Chechnya, resulting in casualties on both sides.

Russia and Chechnya stopped fighting under a ceasefire signed last August and Russia pulled all its forces out, but peace talks are bogged down over Chechnya's political status. Chechnya wants full independence but Russia rules this out.
